description: Parallel Sessions, renewal, account binding, rotation, narrowing, and sign-out.

cases.description: A Session starts signed out: a DPoP token with expires_in > 0 (hours, not days), no scope, no Session named: its key names it.
An account request with no access token gets a 401 challenge with scope and no error code, read as insufficient_scope (§7).
A resource the company doesn't serve is invalid_target (RFC 8707, §4.5).
A service refusing a token not issued for it answers invalid_token with resource_metadata, and the agent reads it again (§4.5).
The same user runs two Sessions at once; each has its own Session Key and both are served.
A sign-in grants no more than the scopes requested and allowed for its type; partial consent shows in scope.
A sign-in asking for a scope the company does not offer is invalid_scope.
The Account Token signs a fresh signed-out Session in at the token endpoint.
After a refresh rotates the Account Token, the old one is invalid_grant; the new one works.
A refresh asking for fewer scopes gets a token with only those.
A refresh asking for a scope the Account Token does not hold is invalid_scope.
Another client_id presenting the Account Token gets invalid_grant.
An Account Token presented at an API as an access token is refused (invalid_token).
After revocation, the Session Token issued before it is handled as signed out on the next request (insufficient_scope).
After revocation, renewal returns a signed-out token for the same Session, and the revoked token is invalid_grant.
Revoking the current, rotated Account Token signs out every Session signed in from the same sign-in, including tokens issued before the rotation; renewing with the assertion is signed out.
Disconnecting the agent at the company revokes its Account Tokens and signs out its Sessions; the agent finds out from invalid_grant and insufficient_scope.
A 429 carries Retry-After, and the SDK reports it without retrying early.

The MCP server's protected resource metadata names it as the resource and the company's issuer among its authorization servers; a server that supports DPoP lists ES256. An unauthenticated call is 401 with one challenge per scheme it accepts, each pointing there.

A Session's token request with resource set to the MCP url returns a token for the same Session, DPoP for a server that supports DPoP and Bearer otherwise; the MCP server accepts it and enforces its scopes.
The MCP server's token is refused at every API, conversation, and operations endpoint; the MCP server refuses the Session's own DPoP token; no token is issued without a proof for another resource.
After revocation the MCP server handles the Session's token for it as signed out (insufficient_scope).
The agent's own browser posts a browser assertion and gets a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie with no lifetime of its own; the website follows the Session's sign-out on the next request.
A join code submitted from another browser, a code used twice, a proof over another code, or a key that names no Session sets no Session cookie (HTTP 400), the two attacks of §9.6 among them.
